rationale: Both candidates have the same endpoint alignment to the target (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect-size evidence and structural signals. PGS002738 shows a stronger reported discrimination proxy (OR top 10% vs rest 1.96 [1.54–2.51]) than PGS002739 (1.76 [1.32–2.34]) and is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with far broader variant coverage (326,000 vs 858 gene-based variants), which is generally more appropriate for a polygenic disorder when comparable PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS002739’s main advantage is AFR evaluation ancestry (vs EUR-only evaluation for PGS002738), but with weaker OR and much sparser construction, the overall support favors PGS002738.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R² (0.00291), with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), allowing a heritability-ceiling sanity check and some transportability context. PGS004477 has a more specific ICD10-style endpoint label (“M13 Other arthritis”) and a genome-wide LDpred2 build with many variants, but it provides no AUROC/R² at all (only an OR=1.20, which is weak-to-moderate) and has unknown covariates, making its predictive performance and comparability much less evidenced on the visible fields.

PGS001267 is the better match to the target trait as a generic ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both directly “Ankylosing spondylitis”), whereas PGS001268 is explicitly a time-to-event (TTE) / survival-style endpoint (“Ankylosing spondylitis (time-to-event)”, phenotyping_reported “TTE ankylosing spondylitis”), which is a noted endpoint-fidelity warning for a generic disease-risk target. Although PGS001268 has slightly higher PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.7346 vs 0.7265; PGS-only R2 0.1023 vs 0.0988), both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same pan-trait UKB framework paper, same method/variants, same covariates, same training and validation context), so the endpoint alignment advantage of PGS001267 outweighs the small metric edge of PGS001268.

PGS002755 is the better-supported standalone PRS for atopic eczema because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and reports a PRS-derived effect size (HR high vs low PRS=1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a very large European evaluation sample (n=337,910) with non-clinical covariates. In contrast, PGS001773 is a very sparse 25-variant score for a narrower endpoint (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis) and its only reported discrimination (AUROC=0.93, R²=0.49) appears to be full-model (not PGS-only) and is therefore not comparable as PRS evidence; it also uses parental ethnicity covariates and has a much smaller validation sample (n=676). Both map to the same EFO trait, but PGS002755 has stronger structural PRS properties and cleaner, more interpretable PRS-specific evidence.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_efo=atopic eczema; phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis) and have similarly clean, non-leaky covariates and identical EUR evaluation size (n=337,910), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either. With metrics essentially tied (HR high vs low PRS 1.249 for PGS002755 vs 1.153 for PGS004587), the structural evidence favors PGS002755: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is generally better suited to a polygenic trait like atopic eczema than a 23-SNP genome-wide-significant score (PGS004587). PGS004587’s listed multi-cohort training is supportive but not enough to outweigh the much sparser construction and weaker HR signal.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = "M13 (Other arthritis)", trait_efo = arthritis), identical training/validation scale (UKB; training n=174,489; validation n=56,192), identical ancestry (EUR-only), identical variant count (1,059,939), and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (no pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2). With metrics missing, the main differentiator is the available effect size: PGS004547 reports a higher OR (1.262) than PGS004477 (1.196), indicating stronger PRS signal on the visible record. Method differences (RFDiseasemetaPRS vs LDpred2) are secondary here given same-publication siblings and the stronger observed OR for PGS004547.

PGS002738 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_efo is exactly "alcohol dependence" and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported are "Alcohol use disorder" (a close clinical synonym). It also shows a reasonably strong PRS signal via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (1.54–2.51), which is more compelling than PGS000201’s modest ΔR²=0.01192 and small beta. While PGS000201 has cleaner disclosed basic covariates and a much larger variant count (1,094,954 vs 326,000), its mapped concept is less faithful (trait_efo "alcohol dependence measurement" and trait_reported "Problematic alcohol use"), making it more like a quantitative/problem-use construct than dependence/AUD. Both lack PRS-only AUC/R², and validation sizes are similar, so endpoint fidelity plus stronger effect-size evidence favors PGS002738.

PGS005254 is the better-supported match to the target trait aortic stenosis: it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo both aortic stenosis) whereas PGS005255 is primarily a hemodynamic measurement score (trait_reported: Mean pressure gradient; trait_efo includes aortic measurement), making it less endpoint-faithful despite sharing the same phenotyping_reported (incident aortic stenosis). Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, PRS-CS, EUR-only dev/eval, same covariates, same validation N, no PRS-only AUC/R2), so the tie-breakers are endpoint fidelity and available effect size/training support; PGS005254 also shows a slightly stronger HR per SD (1.64 vs 1.53) and larger training sample (205,483 vs 98,645), reinforcing the choice.

PGS001268 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance evidence for ankylosing spondylitis: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7346 and PGS-only R²=0.10232 (plus CIs), enabling a clean PRS comparison, whereas PGS002089 provides no AUC/R² and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919), which is less standard and harder to benchmark. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (same EFO; PGS002089 is generic AS, PGS001268 is time-to-event AS, a mild mismatch penalty but not disqualifying). Both are UKB-based framework/portability-style scores, but PGS002089’s stronger method/variant count (LDpred2, 22k variants) cannot outweigh the lack of PRS-only metrics versus PGS001268’s directly reported PRS-only discrimination.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ankylosing spondylitis) and use only basic covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). PGS001267 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R2=0.0988 in Europeans, whereas PGS002089 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919) and no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its predictive strength harder to assess. Although PGS002089 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with many variants (22,026) and has some multi-ancestry evaluation, the lack of standard PRS-only metrics is a key evidence gap versus PGS001267’s directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R2.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo aortic stenosis; incident aortic stenosis phenotyping) and are EUR-trained/EUR-evaluated with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so we rely on effect-size evidence and covariate comparability. PGS005254 reports a clear per-SD HR=1.64 with CI (1.50–1.78) under relatively basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs), giving cleaner PRS signal isolation. PGS005252 reports a higher HR (1.92) but without CI and its only discrimination metric is a full-model C-index=0.87 alongside a heavy comorbidity/clinical covariate set (T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), making the 0.87 largely non-comparable and potentially covariate-driven. Training/validation sizes differ but are weak tie-breakers here; overall PGS005254 has cleaner, better-supported PRS-specific evidence.

PGS005252 is the better-supported match to the target trait (aortic stenosis): its trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are directly aligned to incident aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is primarily a valve-function quantitative trait score (trait_reported="Mean pressure gradient"; trait_efo includes "aortic measurement"), making endpoint fidelity weaker despite mentioning incident AS in phenotyping. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on available evidence: PGS005252 shows a stronger effect size (HR 1.92 vs 1.53 for PGS005255). Although PGS005252’s reported C-index 0.87 is a full-model metric and likely covariate-inflated (it uses many clinical covariates), it still provides some supportive discrimination context; PGS005255 has no discrimination metric at all. Both are EUR-only dev/eval and have similar genome-wide variant counts, so those do not differentiate. Overall, stronger disease-endpoint alignment plus stronger HR favors PGS005252.

PGS002739 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_reported="Alcohol use disorder", trait_efo="alcohol dependence", and phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder". It also provides a clear case-control style discrimination signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76, 95% CI 1.32–2.34) in an African American evaluation cohort, indicating meaningful stratification. In contrast, PGS000201 is more phenotype-adjacent (trait_reported="Problematic alcohol use"; phenotyping is DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed) rather than a direct AUD diagnosis label, and its only comparable performance evidence is a small incremental ΔR²=0.01192 (with β=0.099), with no PRS-only AUC/R². PGS000201 does have cleaner disclosed covariates and a larger genome-wide variant set, but the stronger endpoint fidelity and more interpretable risk stratification metric favor PGS002739 overall.

PGS001344 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R²=0.05973 (no covariates), enabling clean comparison and passing the asthma heritability-ceiling sanity check (well below h2_liability~0.15). In contrast, PGS002727 lacks PGS-only AUC/R² and only shows full-model AUROC=0.66/R²=0.04, which is not a valid substitute for PRS-only performance; its strong OR=1.57 is supportive but doesn’t compensate for missing PRS-only metrics. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (asthma), though PGS002727 is pediatric-specific while PGS001344 is general doctor-diagnosed asthma. PGS002727 has a disease-focused pediatric-asthma publication and broader evaluation ancestries, but given the absence of PRS-only metrics and unknown covariates, the more directly comparable PRS-only evidence in PGS001344 makes it the stronger catalog-supported choice here.

PGS001782 is better supported structurally for asthma PRS use: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (884,043) and is developed across many biobanks (global multi-cohort context), which is generally more reliable than the pan-trait UKB sparse-framework archetype of PGS001344 (snpnet; 6,139 variants; single-cohort UKB development). While PGS001344 reports slightly higher PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only R2=0.0597 and AUROC=0.6457 vs PGS001782 covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.0488, no PGS-only AUROC), that advantage is modest and comes from the known “813 traits” framework paper that tends to generalize worse externally. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (doctor-diagnosed asthma vs asthma), covariates are similarly basic, so the decision leans on study archetype + method/coverage, favoring PGS001782 despite its smaller EUR validation n (7,128 vs 19,857).

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R² (0.00291), allowing a clean PRS signal check (and it stays well below the arthritis heritability ceiling). It also has clearly stated basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and broader evaluation ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), which is supportive for transportability. In contrast, PGS004547 has a more specific reported endpoint label (ICD10 M13 other arthritis) and a genome-wide variant count, but it provides no AUROC/R² at all (only OR=1.26, suggesting weak-to-moderate signal) and has unknown covariates, making its predictive performance and comparability harder to judge.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo are identical AAA), but PGS003972 has stronger structural and study-support signals: it is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with ~1.1M variants developed from a large multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis (many cohorts listed), whereas PGS000753 is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants from a more limited development context. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS003972’s reported AUROC=0.69 is a full-model metric and cannot be used as a PRS-comparable advantage; however, PGS000753’s OR=1.37 per SD is only moderate and does not outweigh the much stronger genome-wide construction and broader disease-focused development of PGS003972. Covariates are basic/known for PGS000753 but unknown for PGS003972, which lowers confidence but is not enough to offset the overall evidence package favoring PGS003972.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = abdominal aortic aneurysm; same method PRS-CS; same variant count; same GWAS/EVAL ancestry pattern; same publication/date), so endpoint fidelity and structural properties do not differentiate. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model metrics are not clean PRS-comparable; however, PGS003973’s reported discrimination is higher (C-index 0.882 with CI) and it explicitly uses only basic demographic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex), which is acceptable and makes the metric at least interpretable as a light-adjusted model. PGS003972 has unknown covariates and a much lower full-model AUROC (0.69), offering weaker and less interpretable support. Validation sample sizes are similar and not decisive.

Both candidates match the target trait (AAA) with coherent trait_reported/trait_efo. Endpoint fidelity is slightly cleaner for PGS003973 (phenotyping_reported: generic “Abdominal aortic aneurysm”) versus PGS000753’s explicitly “Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm,” which is a narrower/survivor-enriched framing. Neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so the reported full-model C-index=0.882 for PGS003973 cannot be treated as PRS-comparable; however, PGS003973 has stronger structural support (PRS-CS with ~1.12M variants) and a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort development set, whereas PGS000753 is a very sparse P+T score (29 variants) with only a moderate per-SD OR=1.37 and no discrimination metrics. Given absent PRS-only metrics on both, the genome-wide shrinkage + much broader variant coverage and multi-cohort disease meta-analysis context make PGS003973 better-supported overall.

PGS001263 is a direct endpoint match to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Atrial flutter”), and it reports clean PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R²=0.025), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling and interpreted without substituting full-model performance. PGS002050 has a broader phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) rather than flutter-specific, and it lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R² entirely (only partial correlation is given), making its predictive evidence less directly comparable for a flutter target despite higher variant count and training N.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same method (GWAS Hits), same EUR-only ancestry distribution, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics with basic covariates). With PRS-comparable metrics absent, small full-model AUROC/R2 differences are weak; however PGS000452 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0487 vs 0.0456) than PGS000456, while PGS000456’s higher top-1% OR does not clearly outweigh the overall slightly stronger discrimination summary in PGS000452. Given the minimal differences and non-PRS-only metrics, confidence is low.

PGS001263 is the better-supported match for the target trait atrial flutter because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all specifically “Atrial flutter,” whereas PGS001339 is a combined phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) and explicitly time-to-event (phenotyping_reported: “TTE atrial fibrillation and flutter”), which is a weaker endpoint match for a generic atrial flutter target. Performance evidence is essentially tied and PRS-comparable in both (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.02517 vs 0.02447; same basic covariates and same training/validation sizes), so phenotype fidelity is the main differentiator. Both are from the same pan-trait UKB framework paper and have similar variant counts, so those do not separate them.

PGS000327 has clean endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to autism spectrum disorder, whereas PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported = "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)") despite the ASD label. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², but PGS000327 provides supportive effect-size evidence (OR=1.33 per SD) and a higher reported R² (0.0245 vs partial R² 0.00546 for PGS002790). Covariates are similarly light in both (PCs/batch vs age+PCs), so the decisive factor is PGS000327’s coherent ASD endpoint plus stronger available discrimination signals.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Disorders of bilirubin excretion; bilirubin metabolism disease), same UKB-only training (n=391,124), same covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), same multi-ancestry evaluation mix and validation size (n=19,924), and essentially identical PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r=0.0716 with overlapping CIs). With metrics unable to differentiate, the structural signal favors PGS002032 because it is a genome-wide shrinkage score with far broader variant coverage (19,768 variants via LDpred2) versus the extremely sparse 22-variant penalized regression score in PGS001824, which is less likely to capture polygenic signal for this trait. Given the otherwise indistinguishable records, this is a method/variant-count tie-break, hence moderate confidence.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the visible full-model AUC/C-index values are not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS005168 is heavily penalized on covariate comparability because it explicitly includes the named clinical risk calculator CHARGE-AF, which is strong risk-wrapper packaging and makes its high C-index (0.8718) likely covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven. PGS005313 uses only basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding that packaging concern, and it provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.79–1.85) plus a cross-ancestry PRS-CSx construction with much larger genome-wide variant coverage (1,271,239 vs 382,963). Despite PGS005168 having a larger validation n and many performance records, the CHARGE-AF augmentation makes its reported discrimination less informative for standalone PRS quality, so PGS005313 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are not strong evidence. Given that, PGS000454 has a marginal edge via slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher pseudo-R² (0.0489 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456’s slightly higher top-1% OR does not outweigh the overall near-tie. Confidence is low because the differences are tiny and metrics are full-model rather than PRS-only.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUCs are not directly comparable as PRS metrics. However, PGS005168’s reported performance is explicitly packaged with the CHARGE-AF clinical risk calculator in the covariates, making its high C-index (0.8718) likely dominated by non-genetic clinical prediction and therefore weak evidence about standalone PRS quality. In contrast, PGS002814 uses only basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) without a named clinical risk tool, so its reported AUROC/R2 (0.74/0.14) is more interpretable for PRS evaluation despite being full-model. Given the strong penalty for risk-calculator packaging and the cleaner covariate design, PGS002814 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates match the target trait well at the concept level (trait_reported/trait_efo = asthma). However, PGS001782 provides a clearly PRS-comparable performance metric: a covariates-regressed-out (PGS-only) Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 (and AUROC=0.659) with explicitly basic covariates (sex, age, 20 PCs), and this R² is below the asthma heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0077; liability h2≈0.1515), making it interpretable. In contrast, PGS002727 reports only full-model metrics (AUROC=0.66, R²=0.04) with covariates listed as Unknown, so its discrimination evidence is less clean/comparable for PRS ranking despite a strong OR=1.57 and very large validation N. Endpoint-wise, PGS002727 is pediatric-asthma-specific (a restriction vs generic asthma), while PGS001782 uses a generic asthma phenotype, better aligned to the broad target. Overall, the cleaner PRS-only R² and clearer covariate specification make PGS001782 better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS000924 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.88697 and PGS-only R²=0.21843 in Europeans, whereas PGS001824 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0716) and no PRS-only AUC/R². Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both, but PGS001824 is a direct bilirubin-excretion disorder while PGS000924 is a combined porphyrin+bilirubin time-to-event phenotype (a mild mismatch). Both are UKB framework-style scores with basic covariates; despite the phenotype penalty, the much clearer PRS-only metric evidence favors PGS000924.

PGS002786 is the better match to the target trait (bipolar disorder): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly bipolar disorder, whereas PGS002788 targets the subtype bipolar II disorder (trait_efo: bipolar II disorder), which is a narrower endpoint. Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, PGC training cohort, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same covariates age+PCs1-3, same validation n=2,524) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R²; both only show small partial R² values from non-disease phenotyping contexts. Although PGS002788 has a slightly higher partial R² (0.00307 vs 0.00251), the metric is not PRS-only and the difference is small, so endpoint fidelity drives the decision.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only ancestry distribution, same training cohort (MGI) and training N (11,734), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation N (11,322). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown (0.632 for both), so discrimination evidence is essentially tied. The only visible edge is that PGS000454 has slightly stronger reported performance in the selected validation record (Nagelkerke pseudo-R² 0.0489 vs 0.0487; OR top 1% vs rest 3.79 vs 3.61), while PGS000452’s GWAS-hits vs P+T method difference is not decisive given the otherwise identical evidence. Hence PGS000454 wins, but confidence is low due to minimal, likely-noise differences.

PGS002786 is the better match to the target trait (bipolar disorder): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly “Bipolar disorder/bipolar disorder,” whereas PGS002787 targets the narrower subtype “Type 1 bipolar disorder/bipolar I disorder.” Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same basic covariates age+PCs1-3) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; the only metric shown is a small partial R² (full-model) that is not PRS-comparable and differs trivially (0.00251 vs 0.00275). Given the endpoint-fidelity priority and the fact that both have non-disease phenotyping_reported fields, the exact trait alignment of PGS002786 is the main differentiator.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and both only use basic covariates (PGS002814: age/sex/PCs; PGS005313: age/sex), so neither shows obvious clinical-risk packaging or leakage. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.74 vs 0.78) are not strictly PRS-comparable; however, with similarly light covariates they are at least directionally informative. PGS005313 has stronger structural support for a polygenic trait (PRS-CSx with ~1.27M variants and explicitly multi-ancestry GWAS input) and broader evaluation ancestry coverage, whereas PGS002814 is a P+T score with far fewer variants (4,520) and is evaluated only in East Asians. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics, the method/variant-count and broader transportability evidence favor PGS005313.

PGS004587 better matches the generic target trait “atopic eczema” via a broad atopic dermatitis endpoint with explicit incident disease phenotyping (“Incident atopic dermatitis”), whereas PGS001773 is restricted to a subtype (“Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis”) and even has a noisy phenotype string. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R²; PGS001773’s very high AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 are full-model metrics (not PRS-comparable) and are further confounded by family-history/ethnicity covariates (father’s and mother’s ethnicity), making the apparent performance advantage non-comparable. PGS004587, while also sparse and lacking PRS-only metrics, provides a direct PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.153) and uses more standard non-clinical covariates, with large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) aligned to its EUR GWAS/EVAL ancestry.

Both candidates align to the target trait (atrial flutter) only as a combined endpoint with atrial fibrillation (same trait_efo). PGS001339 provides cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.613 and PGS-only R2=0.02447 (and incremental AUROC), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling and interpreted as PRS signal rather than covariate-driven full-model performance. PGS002050 lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2 entirely (only partial correlation is given), making its predictive support less directly comparable despite larger variant count and training N. Covariates are basic in both, and ancestry evaluation breadth is similar, so the decisive difference is the availability of explicit PGS-only metrics in PGS001339 versus missing comparable metrics in PGS002050.

PGS002032 is the better-supported choice for the target trait (bilirubin metabolism disease) because its phenotype is a direct match without extra trait bundling (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: “Disorders of bilirubin excretion” mapped to bilirubin metabolism disease), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with a large variant set (LDpred2; 19,768 variants) plus explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EUR/GME/SAS), which is supportive for portability. PGS000924, while it reports explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely sparse 5-variant model and a time-to-event composite phenotype that also includes porphyrin metabolism disease, reducing endpoint fidelity to bilirubin metabolism disease and raising generalizability concerns typical of that framework family. Confidence is moderate because PGS002032 lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R², but the endpoint coherence and stronger structural properties outweigh PGS000924’s framework/sparsity and phenotype-bundling drawbacks.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity to celiac disease (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not PRS-comparable). With metrics essentially non-comparable, structural evidence favors PGS000040: it uses many more variants (228 vs 53), consistent with capturing more polygenic signal, and shows a slightly higher reported AUROC (0.90 vs 0.879), though discounted as full-model. PGS000316’s much larger validation sample size is only a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the stronger model structure/variant coverage of PGS000040. Confidence is moderate because both rely on full-model AUROC with unknown covariates.

PGS001301 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.82867; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.14224) with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and includes some non-EUR evaluation (AFR/SAS). In contrast, PGS000316 only reports a full-model AUROC (0.879) with no PGS-only AUC/R2 and unknown covariates, making its discrimination largely non-comparable for PRS ranking despite a clean celiac endpoint label. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (PGS000316 exact ‘Coeliac disease’ vs PGS001301 ‘Malabsorption/coeliac disease’), but the lack of PRS-only performance evidence in PGS000316 is the decisive weakness.

Both candidates are near-clones: same publication, same SDPR method, similar genome-wide variant counts (~935k), same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), and both lack PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R²; only small partial R² values). The main differentiator is endpoint fidelity to the target trait “bipolar disorder”: PGS002787 targets bipolar I disorder (Type 1), which is closer to the generic bipolar disorder concept than PGS002788’s bipolar II disorder (Type 2). The slightly higher partial R² for PGS002788 (0.00307 vs 0.00275) is a full/partial-model metric difference of marginal magnitude and not a clean PRS-only advantage, so it doesn’t outweigh the closer trait alignment of PGS002787.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; cervical cancer endpoints). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model C-index is only weakly informative. Both candidates match the target well (trait_efo cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident cervical cancer; EUR evaluation). Both candidates align well to the target trait (trait_efo cervical carcinoma; trait_reported cervical cancer) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model C-index/AUROC are not cleanly comparable. Therefore PGS000073 is better-supported overall, with moderate confidence due to reliance on full-model metrics rather than PRS-only metrics.

PGS005090 is better supported for the target CKD endpoint because it is explicitly a CKD-focused study in Black American populations with coherent AFR-only GWAS and AFR-only evaluation (MVP/REGARDS; eval n=67,819), and it reports a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.41, 1.14–1.76). Both candidates lack PGS-only AUC/R2, and PGS005090’s reported AUROC=0.9 appears to be full-model (and includes diabetes as a covariate), so the decision rests mainly on study/endpoint focus and effect-size strength, favoring PGS005090.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to COPD (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match), come from the same publication, use the same method (PRS-CS-auto), and are evaluated in EUR only, so phenotype and study-context do not differentiate them. Variant count and validation N differences are not decisive here. Therefore PGS001783 is better supported by the cleaner PRS-only performance evidence.

PGS004621 is the better-supported match to the target trait (cirrhosis of liver): its trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are directly “cirrhosis,” whereas PGS000704 is explicitly restricted to the subtype “alcoholic cirrhosis” (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), which is a meaningful endpoint mismatch for a generic cirrhosis target. Given the lack of PRS-comparable metrics, structural/study-design signals dominate: PGS004621 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and is developed/validated in a large multi-cohort biobank set with very large EUR evaluation (n≈1,153,995), which is generally more robust for polygenic prediction than PGS000726’s 12 genome-wide significant SNP score. Although PGS000726 reports a stronger tail-contrast OR (top 20% vs bottom 20% OR=2.26), it remains a very sparse score with smaller validation (n≈30,469) and no PRS-only discrimination metrics, so overall support favors PGS004621.

Both candidates match the target trait (CKD stage ≥3) at the trait_reported/trait_efo level, but PGS002237 has clearer endpoint fidelity via phenotyping_reported (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2, explicitly stage 3+), whereas PGS005090’s phenotyping_reported is vague (“Chronic kidney disease”). Although PGS005090 uses a stronger shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and more variants, its performance evidence is largely tied to a high full-model AUROC (0.9) with only basic covariates and lacks training sample size, while PGS002237 comes from a large, disease-focused study with explicit stage-3+ definition and multi-ancestry validation, making it better-supported overall for generic CKD deployment.

Both candidates are well-aligned to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Coronary artery disease”) and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so the decision rests on effect-size evidence and study/transport signals. Overall, stronger phenotype alignment plus more externally oriented development support PGS000726.

PGS001301 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.82867 and PGS-only R²=0.14224 (no covariates), with basic covariates listed and a European selected validation record. PGS000040 has endpoint-fidelity (pure coeliac disease) but lacks any PGS-only metrics; the only visible AUROC=0.9 appears as a full-model/classification AUROC and cannot be treated as a comparable PRS metric per the provided policy. While PGS001301 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a negative signal) and has a slightly broader/less specific reported phenotype label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), it still maps to celiac disease and provides cleaner, directly comparable PRS-only performance evidence than PGS000040.

PGS001783 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance and structural signals for COPD: it reports a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.0381, which is materially stronger than PGS001332’s PGS-only R2=0.00235 and PGS-only AUROC=0.5397 (weak discrimination). PGS001783 also uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with very large variant coverage (884,139 vs 482), consistent with capturing polygenic signal for COPD, and its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0388). Although PGS001783 has smaller EUR evaluation n (7,128 vs 67,425) and lacks a PGS-only AUROC, the much stronger PRS-only R2 and more robust study/method package outweigh those advantages for PGS001332.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all corneal dystrophy), come from the same UKB portability publication, have identical training size, covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), same UKB-only training cohort and training N, same ancestry distribution and validation sample size, and essentially identical PRS performance evidence (partial-r 0.0563 for PGS002034 vs 0.0562 for PGS001826 with overlapping CIs). PGS005170 is the better match to the target trait dementia: it explicitly targets all-cause dementia with incident all-cause dementia phenotyping, whereas PGS002249 is an Alzheimer’s disease PRS (trait_efo Alzheimer disease) even though its phenotyping is incident dementia, creating a concept mismatch for an all-dementia target. Both candidates target the same trait (dilated cardiomyopathy) with the same method (PRS-CS) and EUR-only evaluation, but PGS004951 provides cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it explicitly reports a univariate (PRS-only) AUC of 0.67 (with CI) and delta PRS/residual R² metrics, whereas PGS004862 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.71/0.05) without any PRS-only metric (full-model AUROC is not a valid substitute). Both candidates target the same endpoint with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Hodgkin's disease / Hodgkins lymphoma), same EUR-only ancestry across GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes (n=736 train; n=775 eval), and the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Both candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity and transportability: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Hodgkin's disease / Hodgkins lymphoma), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same training cohort (MGI) with n=736 and same validation size (n=775), and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). PGS002728 is the better-supported choice for the target trait hip osteoarthritis because its concept alignment is direct (trait_reported="Hip osteoarthritis", trait_efo="osteoarthritis, hip"), whereas PGS002750 is primarily framed as the surgical/treatment proxy endpoint (trait_reported="Total hip replacement", trait_efo includes arthroplasty). With no PGS-only AUC/R2 available for either, the cleaner covariate design plus genome-wide construction favors PGS004911.

PGS005265 is better supported for the target hyperthyroidism because its endpoint (Graves’ disease) is a clinically dominant subtype of hyperthyroidism and is developed/validated in a disease-focused, multi-biobank context (AllofUs, FinnGen, UKB, MVP, etc.) with multi-ancestry evaluation listed and a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.63), which is meaningful PRS evidence even without PGS-only AUC/R2. Given the framework penalty and stronger disease-focused multi-cohort support plus OR evidence, PGS005265 edges out despite missing PRS-only AUC/R2 (so confidence is not high).

Both candidates map cleanly to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo are hypothyroidism). However, PGS005218’s only visible discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.859 while explicitly adjusting for strong near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), making that AUROC largely non-comparable and potentially covariate-driven with no PGS-only AUC/R2 reported. Given the heavy biomarker adjustment in PGS005218 and the presence of a strong PRS effect size in PGS004935, PGS004935 is better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS002763 is the better-supported choice for the target trait hip osteoarthritis because its endpoint fidelity is direct: phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Hip osteoarthritis,” matching trait_reported/trait_efo. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS002728’s AUROC=0.66 is a full-model metric (and not comparable as PRS performance), leaving it with no clean PRS-discrimination evidence. Both are EUR-only evaluation; PGS002728 has multi-cohort development listed, but that does not outweigh the clearer phenotype match and stronger PRS-structure/effect-size evidence for PGS002763.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all hypertrophic cardiomyopathy). However, PGS000739’s reported AUROC=0.821 is a full-model metric with heavy clinical covariates (obesity, HTN, AF, CAD) plus rare-variant carrier status, making the discrimination largely non-comparable to a standalone PRS and potentially covariate-driven. PGS004910 also only reports full-model metrics (AUROC=0.73, R²=0.031) but uses much cleaner/basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10) and provides PRS-relevant effect sizes (HR 1.97; OR 1.26; high-vs-median tertile OR 5.5). Structurally it is a genome-wide shrinkage PRS-CS score with 374,190 variants versus 27 GWAS hits for PGS000739, which is generally better aligned with capturing polygenic signal for HCM. Given the covariate-leakage concern in PGS000739 and the cleaner design plus stronger PRS structure in PGS004910, PGS004910 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), study context (same UKB portability paper), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and evaluation ancestry mix/validation N (n=19,883). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either, the main differentiators are the PRS-comparable metric available (partial-r) and structural signals. PGS002031 has slightly higher partial correlation (0.1355 vs 0.1307) and is a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (6,713 vs 654), which is generally favorable for capturing polygenic signal when other fields are equal. The advantage is modest, hence Moderate confidence.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same Nat Genet paper with identical endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; trait_efo matches), identical basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), identical EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same development cohorts, and same validation size (n=343,182). PGS000114 is the better match to the target trait (juvenile idiopathic arthritis): its trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to the broad JIA endpoint, whereas PGS000325 is explicitly for the oligoarticular JIA subtype (endpoint mismatch for a generic JIA target). Both candidates come from the same disease-focused publication, use the same method (SparSNP), have identical basic covariates (sex, PCs 1–10), and are EUR-only in development/evaluation, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC), so the higher full-model AUROC in PGS000325 (0.80 vs 0.738) is discounted and not enough to outweigh the endpoint-fidelity advantage of PGS000114.

PGS005266 is better supported for the target hyperthyroidism because its endpoint is Graves’ disease (the dominant autoimmune cause of clinical hyperthyroidism) with coherent phenotype fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all Graves’) and it comes from a disease-focused, multi-biobank study with broad external validation context (many cohorts; eval includes multiple ancestries; n=94,651). In contrast, PGS001043 is an exact-label match (hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis) and does report clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6323; PGS R2 0.0216, below the heritability ceiling), but it is from the known pan-trait UKB ‘813 traits’ sparse snpnet framework with very few variants (69) and single-biobank development, a pattern associated with weaker external transportability; its incremental/full-model metrics also suggest much of the discrimination is covariate-driven. Net: disease-focused multi-cohort Graves PRS with strong OR outweighs the framework sparse UKB score despite the latter’s PRS-only AUC availability.

PGS000114 is the better match to the target trait (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) because its trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to the umbrella JIA endpoint, whereas PGS000326 is explicitly a subtype score (RF-negative polyarticular JIA) with a narrower phenotyping_reported. Neither candidate provides PRS-only AUC/R2 (both only show full-model AUROC with the same basic covariates: sex and PCs), so performance is hard to compare; the small AUROC difference (0.738 vs 0.76) is not decisive. With similar ancestry (EUR-only), method (SparSNP), and cohorts, the broader endpoint fidelity plus stronger reported OR per SD (2.085 vs 1.51) and higher variant count (26 vs 12) favor PGS000114.

PGS004908 is better supported for the target trait (kidney cancer) because its endpoint is a direct kidney cancer diagnosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Kidney cancer”) and it comes from a kidney-cancer–focused multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with a substantially larger variant set (107 vs 19). While neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R² (so full-model AUROC values are not comparable PRS metrics), PGS004908 provides stronger PRS-specific evidence via a higher per-SD effect size (OR=1.5) than PGS000787 (HR=1.15), suggesting materially stronger standalone genetic signal. PGS000787 is also from a pan-cancer risk-factor integration context and uses an incident-only endpoint, with performance largely presented as full-model metrics alongside multiple non-genetic risk factors, making its reported discrimination less informative for PRS quality than the stronger effect-size evidence in PGS004908.

Both candidates match the target conceptually (trait_reported/trait_efo are knee osteoarthritis) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so candidate_b’s full-model AUROC=0.66 (with Age/sex/BMI covariates) is not a comparable PRS metric and can’t be used as a decisive advantage. PGS004908 is better supported for the target “kidney cancer” because its endpoint is a direct kidney cancer diagnosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: “Kidney cancer”) and it comes from a kidney-cancer-focused multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; BBJ/FinnGen/NCI), whereas PGS000076 is from a cross-cancer evaluation framework and uses an incident-only endpoint (“Incident kidney cancer”), which is a mild mismatch for generic kidney cancer risk. Covariate sets are broadly similar epidemiologic adjustments in both, so they don’t rescue PGS000076. Both candidates map cleanly to the target (trait_efo is osteoarthritis, knee; phenotyping is knee OA/gonarthrosis) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must lean on structural/study-design signals and effect sizes. Both candidates are endpoint-aligned to the target (trait_reported kidney cancer; trait_efo renal cell carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident kidney cancer), use the same covariates, same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same validation sample size (n=391,610), and show essentially identical full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.722; C-index ~0.723–0.724) and similar HR per SD (1.16 for PGS000076 vs 1.15 for PGS000787). PGS000788 is better supported for the target lymphoid leukemia because its endpoint fidelity is strong and explicit (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo matches), and it shows a materially stronger PRS signal via effect size (HR per SD 1.7) with only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). Both candidates have identical endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo = lung cancer/lung carcinoma; phenotyping_reported = incident lung cancer), identical ancestry context (EUR GWAS and EUR evaluation), identical covariate-heavy evaluation (includes family history plus detailed smoking variables and interactions), and essentially identical reported discrimination/effect size (full-model AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849; HR per SD ~1.16–1.17). Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported lung cancer; trait_efo lung carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident lung cancer; EUR GWAS/EVAL). Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo are hypothyroidism). Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma), use the same method (genome-wide significant variants) with the same variant count (23), and are EUR-only in GWAS and evaluation. Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to hypothyroidism (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and both are EUR-trained/evaluated in UKB, with similar per-SD effect sizes (PGS004935 OR=1.50 vs PGS002766 OR=1.47). Both candidates are essentially matched on endpoint fidelity (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; EFO Nasal Cavity Polyp), ancestry (EUR dev/eval), cohorts (UKB), training/validation sizes, and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (no pgs_only_auc/r2). Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same trait_reported/trait_efo and same phenotyping_reported string), same method (PRSCS), same evaluation ancestry distribution (MAE 100%), same validation sample size (n=94,651), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC is shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo match; phenotyping_reported identical aside from a typo) and come from the same publication with the same evaluation ancestry mix and validation sample size (n=94,651), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS comparator). Both candidates target the same disease concept (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) and use the same method/variant count (GWAS-significant, 22 variants) with the same listed development cohorts, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator). Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait snpnet framework paper with identical training size (n=269,704), covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), ancestry distribution, and validation size (n=24,905), so the main differentiator is endpoint fidelity vs small PRS-only metric differences. Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) and both are sparse 22-variant GWAS-hit style scores with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so full-model AUROC is not a clean differentiator. Both candidates have good endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Osteoporosis), but PGS002768 is better-supported structurally and by PRS-relevant evidence: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) in a sizeable EUR validation (n=39,444) with only basic covariates. Despite PGS002768 lacking explicit PGS-only AUC/R2, the combination of cleaner PRS signal (OR) and stronger polygenic architecture capture makes it the stronger choice over the sparse framework score.

Both candidates are from the same Lancet Neurol PD GWAS meta-analysis, with identical trait/phenotyping alignment (Parkinson’s disease), identical basic covariates (PCs 1–5, age, sex), identical training sample size (n=1,473,098) and validation size (n=999), so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. Structurally, PGS000903 is a denser C+T score with far more variants (1,805 vs 90 GWAS hits), which is a positive tie-break when PRS-only metrics are absent. Therefore PGS000903 is better supported on the visible fields.

PGS002768 is the better-supported choice for generic osteoporosis risk because its endpoint is a direct osteoporosis diagnosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Osteoporosis”) and it comes from a disease-focused cross-disease evaluation paper with clean basic covariates; it also provides a moderate PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with very large variant coverage. In contrast, PGS001274 is from the known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”), with a time-to-event, subtype-like endpoint (“osteoporosis without pathological fracture (TTE)”) that is less faithful to the broad target; while it reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 (0.576 and 0.00945), these are modest and the very high full-model AUROC is largely covariate-driven (incremental AUROC only 0.00777). Overall, endpoint fidelity + study archetype/method structure favor PGS002768 despite missing PRS-only AUC/R2.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), study context (same UKB portability paper), training size (n=391,124), covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.), ancestry distribution, and validation size (n=19,668), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. Given the small metric gap and overlapping CIs, confidence is moderate rather than high.

Both candidates align to the target trait (Parkinson disease) at trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000902 has a cleaner generic disease endpoint (“Parkinson’s disease”) whereas PGS003763 is explicitly “Incident Parkinson Disease” in a time-to-event framing, which is a mild endpoint restriction for a generic PD-risk target. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC (0.651) in PGS000902 is not a strong differentiator, but PGS003763 at least provides an HR (1.72 high vs low tertile) while PGS000902 lacks PRS-isolating effect sizes; still, PGS000902 is supported by a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis context (multiple PD cohorts listed) and a larger, more comprehensive GWAS-hits set (90 vs 44 variants), while PGS003763 has no training/development cohort information and looks more like an application study. Overall, the stronger disease-focused development evidence and broader score construction favor PGS000902 despite limited comparable performance metrics in both.

PGS005217 is better supported for the target concept despite a slight label mismatch (peripheral artery disease vs peripheral vascular disease): its phenotyping is a clear clinical endpoint (incident PAD) and it comes from a disease-focused PAD study with broad multi-ancestry evaluation and a large validation sample (n=304,294). Both candidates have clean endpoint fidelity for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all psoriasis) and both are UKB-derived framework-style scores with only basic demographic/PC covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Hodgkin's disease; trait_efo = Hodgkins lymphoma), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes (n=736 train; n=775 eval), and similarly clean/basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Both candidates align to the target conceptually (trait_reported/trait_efo = Parkinson’s disease/Parkinson disease), but PGS000903 has stronger overall support on the visible fields: it is a disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS-derived score with explicit training/development cohorts listed (23andMe, IPDGC, UKB, etc.), a much richer polygenic construction (1805 variants via C+T vs 44 genome-wide significant SNPs for PGS003763), and it reports multiple performance signals including an OR top-vs-bottom quartile of 6.25 (plus beta/SE) alongside a full-model AUROC/R² (not PRS-only, but still informative given basic covariates age/sex/PCs). Both candidates come from the same pan-trait UKB sparse snpnet framework paper, with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (269,704), evaluation ancestry mix, validation N (67,425), and similarly clean/basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Both candidates are near-clones: same schizophrenia endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same ancestry distribution (GWAS EAS+EUR; EUR-only evaluation), same basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC reported, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Both candidates are near-clones: same schizophrenia endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match), same method (PRS-CS), same ancestry distribution (GWAS mostly EUR with small EAS; EUR-only evaluation), and same basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/platform/batch) with no obvious leakage. PGS000461 is better supported on visible, cleaner evaluation metadata: it discloses basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and provides richer performance context (AUROC with CI, pseudo-R², Brier, and top-1% OR), whereas PGS000731 has covariates listed as “Unknown” and provides only a point AUROC and per-SD OR. With comparable variant counts (13 vs 14) and both EUR-only evaluation, the transparency and breadth of reported evaluation metrics favor PGS000461.

PGS003586 has clearly better endpoint fidelity to the target trait preeclampsia: its phenotyping_reported is "Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia" and trait_reported/efo both match preeclampsia, whereas PGS004593’s phenotyping_reported is "Gestational hypertension," a related but non-identical hypertensive disorder of pregnancy (endpoint mismatch penalty). Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect-size and study support matter more: PGS003586 shows a stronger per-SD association (OR 1.31) than PGS004593 (HR 1.16), suggesting stronger PRS signal. PGS003586 also provides explicit multi-cohort training/development cohorts and a defined training sample size, while PGS004593 lists no training cohorts and has N/A training size, reducing support/traceability despite its larger validation N. Both use PRS-CS with similar variant counts and basic covariates, so the decision is driven by phenotype alignment and stronger effect-size evidence favoring PGS003586.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all psoriasis) and both are UKB-derived framework-style scores with only basic covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). However, PGS001312 provides directly PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6916 and PGS-only R2=0.0523) whereas PGS002083 reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0632) and has no PRS-only AUC/R2, making its predictive evidence less comparable and less interpretable for PRS quality ranking. Although PGS002083 uses many more variants and a genome-wide shrinkage method, the absence of PRS-comparable discrimination metrics on the record leaves weaker visible support than PGS001312’s explicit PGS-only AUC/R2.

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Squamous cell carcinoma”) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the visible AUROC values are full-model and not cleanly comparable as PRS metrics. Given that, PGS000731 has slightly stronger reported discrimination/effect size evidence (full-model AUROC 0.605; OR 1.44 [1.41–1.48]) than PGS000120 (AUROC 0.59 [0.56–0.61]; OR 1.4 [1.31–1.5]) and a larger validation sample (88,924 vs 20,468). PGS000120 does have explicitly basic covariates listed (age/sex/batch/PCs) whereas PGS000731’s covariates are unknown, which tempers confidence; overall the evidence edge is modest, hence low confidence.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry (EUR-only), same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and similarly clean/basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use PRS-comparable metrics and must lean on the available validation evidence. PGS000471 shows materially stronger reported discrimination and effect size in the selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.569 vs 0.524; Nagelkerke R² 0.0255 vs 0.00141; OR per SD 1.401 vs 1.09; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77 vs 1.48) compared with PGS000469. Although PGS000469 uses a genome-wide method with many variants, within this same-study/same-endpoint comparison the empirical performance/effect-size evidence favors PGS000471.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given that, the main differentiator is the observed validation evidence: PGS000470 shows higher full-model AUROC (0.557 vs 0.524), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0154 vs 0.00141), and stronger effect sizes (per-SD OR 1.308 vs 1.09; top 1% OR 2.45 vs 1.48). Although PGS000469 uses a genome-wide PRS-CS with many variants, its weaker empirical performance/effect-size signals in the same setting make PGS000470 better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ulcerative colitis) and use only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), so endpoint fidelity and leakage risk are similar. However, PGS001306 is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with a very small SNP set (179) and only modest PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.630, PGS R2 0.020), whereas PGS004253 is a disease-focused UC score using a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2-auto; 744,575 variants) and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.84), which is meaningful PRS discrimination evidence even though it lacks explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 (its 0.66 AUROC is full-model and not directly comparable). Given the framework penalty and sparsity of PGS001306 versus the stronger structural properties and effect-size evidence for PGS004253, PGS004253 is better supported overall, with moderate confidence due to missing PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort (MGI), same training N (6,005), same validation N (5,500), and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given this near-clone setting, PGS000471 is better supported by consistently stronger reported validation signals: higher AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557), higher pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154), stronger top-1% vs rest OR (3.77 vs 2.45), and higher per-SD OR (1.401 vs 1.308). It also uses a shrinkage-style method (lassosum) and includes slightly more variants (7 vs 5), aligning with the stronger empirical performance compared with PGS000470.

PGS001030 is a direct match to the target umbrella trait (“Pulmonary fibrosis” in trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported) and, crucially, reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates = 0.6252; PGS R2 no covariates = 0.0142), giving cleaner comparable evidence of standalone PRS signal. PGS001791 is endpoint-narrower (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis rather than pulmonary fibrosis) and only provides a covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.005929) with no PRS-only AUROC; its visible AUROC (0.758) is full-model and not comparable as PRS performance. Although PGS001791 has a stronger structural setup (genome-wide PRS-CS-auto with many variants and multi-biobank development), the available PRS-comparable metrics favor PGS001030, and both use only basic demographic/PC covariates without obvious clinical leakage.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), identical method (PRS-CS), identical ancestry context (GWAS EAS+EUR; EUR-only evaluation), and similarly clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC is not a clean PRS-comparable metric; however, given covariates are the same, the higher reported AUROC in PGS000135 (0.74 vs 0.60 for PGS000133) is at least supportive within this sibling comparison. PGS000135 also has a substantially higher variant count (972,439 vs 604,645), a positive within-method structural signal. PGS000133’s only countervailing advantage is a larger validation sample (33,694 vs 9,569) and an OR=1.691 effect size, but PGS000135 is better supported overall by stronger discrimination evidence (even if full-model) plus higher genome-wide coverage.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Squamous cell carcinoma”), identical ancestry scope (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), and similarly basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator). Given that, PGS000461 has slightly stronger PRS signal evidence via effect sizes (OR per SD 1.491 vs 1.4 for PGS000120) and a marginally higher full-model AUROC (0.599 vs 0.59) with similarly light covariates; it also reports additional calibration/fit metrics (Nagelkerke R², Brier, top-1% OR), providing a richer validation evidence package than PGS000120. PGS000120’s larger validation N does not outweigh the stronger effect-size evidence and richer metrics in PGS000461.

Both candidates have identical endpoint alignment (trait_reported Bladder cancer; trait_efo urinary bladder carcinoma; phenotyping_reported Cancer of bladder), identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so the very similar full-model AUROC 0.571 vs 0.572 is not a reliable differentiator). Given that, structural/effect-size evidence breaks the tie: PGS000613 uses P+T with slightly more variants (15 vs 13) and shows a much stronger extreme-risk separation (OR top 1% vs rest 2.91 vs 1.47) with similar per-SD OR (~1.30 in both). Training/validation sizes differ but are weak signals; overall PGS000613 has the more supportive discrimination evidence within this near-clone pair.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same trait_reported/trait_efo, same phenotyping_reported, same method and 13 variants, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, and same basic covariates), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/Nagelkerke R², which are not clean PRS-comparable). PGS000610 has a trivially higher full-model AUROC (0.572 vs 0.567) and pseudo-R² (0.013 vs 0.0114), but these small differences are essentially noise given identical covariates and lack of PRS-only metrics; moreover its top-1% OR is weaker and imprecise (1.47, CI 0.779–2.77) versus PGS000611 (2.66, CI 1.79–3.93). With endpoint fidelity and structure otherwise identical, the stronger and more stable tail-risk separation plus larger training/validation samples in PGS000611 provide slightly better support overall.

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment to ulcerative colitis (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and use only basic demographic/PC-style covariates (no obvious clinical-risk packaging). However, PGS004253 is supported by stronger PRS-relevant evidence: it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.84, 95% CI 1.76–1.93), which is a meaningful indicator of discriminative power even though its AUROC shown (0.66) is a full-model metric and not PRS-only. Structurally it is a genome-wide shrinkage score (LDpred2-auto) with very large variant coverage (744,575), which is generally more appropriate for a polygenic autoimmune trait than the very sparse portability-framework score PGS001855 (penalized regression, 1,505 variants) from a “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” study; PGS001855’s only comparable performance signal is a modest partial correlation (partial-r=0.0625). While PGS001855 has broader multi-ancestry evaluation, the framework/portability context plus sparse construction and weaker metric evidence make it less well-supported overall than PGS004253.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Ulcerative colitis”) and both are UKB-derived framework/portability-style scores with only basic demographic/PC covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). The key differentiator is that PGS001306 reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.63006 and PGS-only R²=0.02036), which are interpretable and pass the heritability-ceiling sanity check (well below h2_liability≈0.2646). In contrast, PGS001855 provides only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0625) and no PGS-only AUROC/R², making its predictive evidence less directly comparable for PRS quality ranking despite larger training N and more variants. Therefore PGS001306 is better-supported on the visible record fields.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Urinary calculus/urolithiasis), same UKB-only development (n=391,124), same covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), same ancestry distribution and validation size (n=19,913), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are (1) PRS-comparable performance proxy and (2) structural method/coverage: PGS002075 has higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0385 vs 0.0323 for PGS001864) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (731,196 vs 5,599), which is generally favored for polygenic traits when other fields are equal. With no cleaner PRS-only metrics available, these modest but consistent advantages make PGS002075 better supported.

PGS001250 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance evidence for urolithiasis: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.56681; PGS R2 0.00592) in Europeans, whereas PGS002075 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r 0.0385) and has no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, making discrimination strength harder to judge. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (PGS002075: “Urinary calculus”/urolithiasis; PGS001250: “calculus of kidney and ureter” TTE mapping to nephrolithiasis/ureterolithiasis), with PGS001250 slightly narrower but still within the urolithiasis spectrum; its time-to-event phenotyping is a mild downside but not enough to outweigh the clearer PRS-only metrics. Both are UKB-based framework-style scores, so study archetype does not differentiate strongly; thus the decisive advantage is PGS001250’s cleaner, directly comparable PRS-only performance reporting.

PGS001864 is the better match to the target trait urolithiasis on endpoint fidelity: its trait_efo is exactly urolithiasis and phenotyping_reported is a direct diagnosis-style endpoint (“Urinary calculus”), whereas PGS001250 is specifically “Calculus of kidney and ureter (time-to-event)” with trait_efo mapped to nephrolithiasis/ureterolithiasis and a TTE endpoint, which is a mild mismatch/packaging relative to generic urolithiasis risk. Although PGS001250 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.5668; PGS R2 0.00592) and PGS001864 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 (only partial-r=0.0323), the reported PRS-only performance for PGS001250 is modest and does not outweigh the cleaner trait alignment plus broader multi-ancestry evaluation coverage shown for PGS001864 (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS vs AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS).

PGS001536 is better supported for vitiligo because it has clear endpoint alignment (trait_efo Vitiligo; phenotyping_reported explicitly “TTE vitiligo”) and, crucially, reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.64193 and PGS-only R² 0.01621) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), staying well below the vitiligo heritability ceiling. In contrast, PGS000738 has a major endpoint/phenotype inconsistency (phenotyping_reported = “Red hair” despite trait_reported Vitiligo), lacks PRS-only AUC/R², and only provides a pseudo R²/full-model-style metric, making its PRS evidence much less clean and comparable despite being from a disease-focused publication.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target (trait_reported=Bladder cancer, trait_efo=urinary bladder carcinoma, phenotyping_reported=Cancer of bladder), come from the same publication, and have the same EUR-only training/validation context and covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given this near-clone setup, PGS000613 has consistently slightly stronger empirical signals in the selected validation record: higher AUROC (0.571 vs 0.567), higher pseudo-R² (0.0125 vs 0.0114), higher top-1% OR (2.91 vs 2.66), and slightly higher per-SD OR (1.301 vs 1.284), plus a marginally larger variant count (15 vs 13). These small but consistently favorable differences make PGS000613 better-supported than PGS000611.

PGS001536 is the better-supported vitiligo PRS because its endpoint is directly vitiligo (phenotyping_reported: "TTE vitiligo") and it reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193; PGS-only R2=0.01621), which are also plausible under the vitiligo heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.17). It also has broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS) with a large validation sample (n=67,425) and only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). In contrast, PGS000760 has a major phenotype mismatch: phenotyping_reported is "anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients" (treatment-induced, different endpoint), provides no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only an HR=1.41 and a meta-analysis p-value), and is evaluated on a much smaller sample (n=1,584) in EUR only.

PGS001795 is the better-supported choice for the target trait “uterine cancer” because its endpoint matches the umbrella phenotype directly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Uterine cancer/uterine carcinoma”), and it reports a PRS-comparable metric (pgs_only_r2 / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 = 0.001948), which is interpretable against the provided low heritability ceiling. In contrast, PGS003381 targets the dominant subtype (endometrial carcinoma) rather than the umbrella uterine cancer label and provides only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.761, R2 0.11) without any PGS-only AUC/R2, making its apparent performance largely non-comparable for PRS ranking despite cleaner covariates. Both are EUR-evaluated, but PGS001795’s explicit PRS-only R2 and exact phenotype alignment outweigh PGS003381’s higher (full-model) AUROC.

PGS003381 is better supported structurally for the target uterine cancer because its endpoint (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported = uterine endometrial carcinoma; trait_efo = endometrial carcinoma) is a clinically dominant subtype of uterine cancer and thus a strong match, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (lassosum) with very large variant coverage (529,365) and a large European validation sample (n=144,479) with only basic covariates (age, PCs). PGS000541 has exact umbrella alignment (malignant neoplasm of uterus; trait_efo = uterine cancer) but is a sparse GWAS-hits score (18 variants) from a repository-style framework paper with much smaller training (n=7,131) and only modest reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.576). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the decision leans on endpoint dominance + stronger method/coverage and validation support favoring PGS003381.

PGS001795 is the better-supported uterine cancer PRS on PRS-comparable evidence and model structure: it reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 (0.001948), whereas PGS000541 provides only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.576; pseudo-R2 0.0133) without a PRS-only AUC/R2, making its discrimination less comparable for PRS ranking. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (uterine cancer/uterine carcinoma vs malignant neoplasm of uterus), and both use only basic demographic/PC-style covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). Structurally, PGS001795 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with ~912k variants and is developed across many biobanks with large EUR evaluation (n=170,276), while PGS000541 is a sparse GWAS-hits score (18 variants) from a repository-style UKB-derived model with much smaller evaluation (n=6,987). Although PGS001795’s PRS-only R2 is small, it is at least explicitly PRS-comparable and aligns with the low heritability ceiling context; PGS000541 lacks that clean PRS-only metric.

PGS000738 is better aligned to the target trait vitiligo on the key endpoint-fidelity field: despite correct trait_reported/trait_efo for both candidates, PGS000738’s phenotyping_reported is not treatment-context-specific, whereas PGS000760 is explicitly tied to an immunotherapy-related phenotype (“anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients”), which is a clear endpoint mismatch/therapy-induced context relative to generic vitiligo risk. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS000738 at least provides a pseudo R² (0.0386) from a vitiligo-focused publication context, while PGS000760 provides only a meta-analysis p-value and an HR (1.41) in a non-vitiligo endpoint setting. Although PGS000760 has a much larger training sample and basic PC covariates, those do not compensate for the explicit phenotype mismatch; thus PGS000738 is the more defensible vitiligo PRS candidate.
